problemStatement.formal: faulhaber_formula : ∑ i ∈ range n, (i : ℚ) ^ p = ∑ i ∈ range (p+1), B_i · C(p+1,i) · n^(p+1-i) / (p+1)
problemStatement.plain: Prove closed-form formulas for sums of consecutive kth powers using Bernoulli numbers (Faulhaber's theorem, Wiedijk #77).
whyMatters: Fundamental result in combinatorics and number theory
Connects finite sums to Bernoulli numbers and polynomials
The identity sum_cubes = (sum)^2 (Nicomachus) is one of the most elegant in mathematics

proven: General Faulhaber formula via Mathlib's Finset.sum_range_pow
Bernoulli polynomial evaluation form: (p+1)·∑i^p = B_{p+1}(n) - B_{p+1}(0)
Odd Bernoulli vanishing: B_{2k+1}=0 for k≥1
Agreement: ℕ formulas match ℚ Faulhaber for k=2,3
knownResults.goal: Complete: general formula + specific cases k=1..7 with 0 sorries

currentState.focus: Complete: 55 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. General Faulhaber + k=1..7 + Bernoulli connection.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: 55 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Comprehensive Faulhaber formula formalization covering: general Bernoulli number formula (from Mathlib), Bernoulli polynomial evaluation form, specific cases k=0..7 with ℕ proofs, Nicomachus theorem, structural properties (monotonicity, upper bounds), verification examples, and full Bernoulli connection section proving B₀=1, B₁=-1/2, odd Bernoulli vanishing, and agreement between ℕ and ℚ formulas.
builtItems: proofs/Proofs/SumOfKthPowers.lean: faulhaber_formula - general Faulhaber via Mathlib
insights: Mathlib's Finset.sum_range_pow directly provides the general Faulhaber formula
Finset.sum_range_pow_eq_bernoulli_sub gives the Bernoulli polynomial form
The ℕ proofs use clever rearrangement to avoid natural number subtraction
nlinarith handles the inductive step for higher powers (k=4..7) automatically
The Bernoulli connection lifts ℕ proofs to ℚ via exact_mod_cast
